terms.s1b: Satoshi Scholar is a non-custodial Bitcoin and Lightning wallet that runs entirely in your browser. We provide software, not a financial service: we never hold your funds, your keys, or any account on your behalf.
terms.s2t: You are in control, and responsible
terms.s2b: Your recovery phrase (and your passkey, if you use one) is the only way to access your funds. If you lose it, nobody, including us, can recover your wallet, and your funds will be permanently lost. Transactions on Bitcoin and Lightning are irreversible.
terms.s3b: Payments are executed by the Breez SDK over the Spark and Lightning networks. Your Lightning address is provided by Breez's LNURL service. Network fees are paid to the network operators; we charge no fees and receive no part of them.
terms.s4b: You may only use the wallet where it is legal to do so, and you are solely responsible for complying with your local laws, including tax obligations.
terms.s5b: The wallet is provided "as is", without warranties of any kind. Bitcoin and Lightning are experimental technologies and the value of bitcoin is volatile. To the maximum extent permitted by law, we are not liable for any loss of funds, profits, or data arising from your use of the wallet.
terms.s6b: We may update these terms from time to time. Continued use of the wallet after an update means you accept the new terms.

privacy.p1b: The wallet has no sign-up and no user accounts. We do not collect, store, or process your name, email, or any other personal information.
privacy.p2t: Your keys never leave your device
privacy.p2b: Your recovery phrase is generated in your browser and stored there encrypted with your password or passkey. It is never sent to any server in any form.
privacy.p3b: To operate, the wallet exchanges payment data (such as invoices and node operations) directly with Breez and Spark infrastructure, and registers your chosen Lightning-address username with the LNURL service. This data identifies your wallet on the network, not your person.
privacy.p4b: If you enable it, your already-encrypted vault is uploaded to a hidden app folder in your own Google Drive. Your browser talks to Google directly; we never see your Drive, your data, or your Google credentials. Google's own privacy policy applies to your Drive.
privacy.p5b: The wallet contains no analytics, trackers, or ads. Preferences such as language and currency are stored locally in your browser.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.a1: You do. Your keys are generated and stored only on your device, and every payment is signed there. Your balance lives in outputs that require two signatures to move: yours and the Spark operators'. Neither side can move funds alone, and you always hold pre-signed Bitcoin transactions that let you withdraw to a regular Bitcoin address without anyone's permission. Nobody else, including us, can move your funds.
faq.a2: Spark is a second layer built on Bitcoin. Your balance is real bitcoin, anchored to the Bitcoin blockchain, but held in a structure that lets you send and receive instantly and for free, without waiting for block confirmations. It is self-custodial: you can always leave Spark and claim your funds on the Bitcoin blockchain on your own.
faq.q3: What is Lightning, and how does this wallet use it?
faq.a3: Lightning is a payment network built on top of Bitcoin that makes payments near-instant and very cheap. You don't run a Lightning node and you don't manage channels: the wallet connects to Lightning through a service provider using atomic swaps, a trade that either completes on both sides or doesn't happen at all, so the provider can never take your funds. You can pay and be paid by any Lightning wallet in the world.
faq.q4: Do I need to be online to receive money?
faq.a4: No. Payments to your Lightning address work even when the app is closed: the payment completes for the sender, and the funds wait for you, locked to your key. The same is true for Spark transfers and for bitcoin sent to your on-chain deposit address. The next time you open the wallet, it finalizes everything automatically.
faq.q5: What if I lose my recovery phrase?
faq.a5: While you can still unlock the wallet on this device, you can reveal the phrase again from the home screen and write it down. If you lose the phrase and access to every device (or your passkey), your funds are permanently lost. There is no reset.
faq.q6: What's the difference between a password and a passkey wallet?
faq.a6: A password wallet stores your phrase on the device, encrypted with a password you type. A passkey wallet derives the wallet from a passkey (fingerprint, face, or device PIN), so there is no password to remember. Both give you a 12-word recovery phrase as the master backup.
faq.a7: An email-like address (name@domain) that others can use to pay you. You get one automatically and can change the name in settings; payments to it arrive straight into your wallet.
faq.a8:
None for us. We do not charge any fees; all costs go directly to the underlying networks and depend on the transaction type:
• Spark to Spark transfers: completely free ($0) and instant.
• Lightning payments: a fixed 0.25% fee plus standard network routing.
• Withdrawing to a Bitcoin address: network fee (sats/vB) calculated as 250 × sats/vB + 750 satoshis. The app shows the total before you confirm.
• Claiming an on-chain deposit: a quoted fee shown before you accept. If network fees are high, the app waits and asks you before paying more.
Our app adds no extra markups and makes no profit from these transactions.
faq.q9: Can I use my wallet on another device?
faq.a9: Yes. Restore it with your 12-word phrase on the new device; that works anywhere. If you created your wallet with a passkey, you can also sign in with that same passkey, but only on this website and only on devices where your platform (iCloud Keychain or Google Password Manager) has synced it. Your fingerprint or face is not the key: it just unlocks the passkey stored on the device. Other wallets can't use it, so always keep your 12 words written down.
faq.q10: What happens if the operators or the service provider disappear?
faq.a10: Your funds are safe. You hold pre-signed Bitcoin transactions that let you withdraw everything to a regular Bitcoin address unilaterally, with no cooperation needed. The withdrawal takes longer than normal (it involves a security waiting period measured in blocks) and costs on-chain fees, but no one can prevent it. Day to day, the providers also can't touch your money; at worst, an outage pauses instant payments until it's resolved.
faq.q11: What happens if this website goes offline?
faq.a11: Your funds live on the Bitcoin and Spark networks, not on this site. With your 12-word phrase you can restore your wallet in any compatible wallet built on the same technology. Even in the extreme case where every server disappears, the pre-signed exit transactions your wallet holds let you recover your funds directly on the Bitcoin blockchain.
